issues.body:
In the `Lint GitHub Actions workflows (advisory findings)` step the body begins `set -uo pipefail`. That enables nounset and pipefail but does NOT disable errexit, which GitHub already set: the default `run` shell is `bash -e {0}`, and an explicit `shell: bash` is `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}`. With pipefail on, `actionlint -no-color .github/workflows/*.yml 2>&1 | tee "$output"` returns 1 whenever actionlint reports findings, and errexit terminates the script on that line.

Consequences:
* `status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}` and the `if (( status > 1 ))` discrimination never execute, so exit 1 (findings) and exit 2/3 (tool failure) produce the identical red step — the exact conflation the workflow header says it prevents ("a broken lane cannot look clean").
* The `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` block and the trailing `exit 0` are unreachable on any run with findings, so the lane produces no finding count and is not advisory at all.

Reproduced locally with the step body verbatim against a fixture that makes actionlint exit 1: under `bash -e` the step exits 1 without printing the post-pipeline marker; same under `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`. The sibling `Self-test actionlint detects an invalid workflow` step handles this correctly with `set +e` / `status=$?` / `set -e`, which shows the hazard was known and just missed here.
issues.fix_hint:
Explicitly clear errexit in this step before the pipeline, e.g.

    set +e
    set -uo pipefail
    output="$RUNNER_TEMP/actionlint.txt"
    actionlint -no-color .github/workflows/*.yml 2>&1 | tee "$output"
    status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

(or keep errexit and neutralise the pipeline with `... | tee "$output" || true`, or wrap it in `if ! actionlint ...; then :; fi`). Also add a regression check that the advisory path is really advisory — e.g. extend the self-test step to run the same command shape over the known-bad fixture and assert the step still reaches the summary/exit-0 path — otherwise this class of bug re-enters silently.
issues.title: Advisory lint step inherits errexit: any finding aborts before the status check, so findings hard-fail and are indistinguishable from tool failure

issues.body:
The workflow declares a bare `merge_group:` trigger. `scripts/tests/test_mergequeue_lane_inventory.py` pins the merge-queue lane inventory in `docs/branch-protection.md` §Merge-queue subset against the live `on:` blocks with SET EQUALITY in both directions, and it is invoked by `.github/workflows/docs-quality.yml:995` — a gating lane.

Run at the PR head:

    FAIL: test_doc_names_exactly_the_merge_group_triggered_workflows
    AssertionError: Items in the second set but not the first: 'actionlint.yml'
    ... Triggers but undocumented: ['actionlint.yml']; documented but does not trigger: []

The test's own message states the contract: "update the prose in the SAME change that adds or removes a merge_group trigger." As it stands this PR reds a gating check.

Separately worth a maintainer decision rather than a silent default: the `pull_request` and `push` triggers are path-filtered to `.github/workflows/**` and `.github/advisory-registry.json`, but `merge_group` carries no filter, so the lane runs on every merge-queue entry and the ci-summary poll loop waits for it on every merge even when no workflow file changed.
issues.fix_hint: Add `actionlint.yml` to the `The lanes that DO trigger on `merge_group` today are:` list in docs/branch-protection.md §Merge-queue subset (noting it is registry-declared advisory), then re-run `python3 scripts/tests/test_mergequeue_lane_inventory.py` until green. If the queue-side run is not wanted, drop the `merge_group:` trigger instead — the PR-head run already covers the diff — and leave the doc list unchanged.
issues.title: merge_group trigger added without updating docs/branch-protection.md — gating docs-quality test test_mergequeue_lane_inventory.py fails

issues.body:
The entry's promotion_criteria says "remove this registry entry so actionlint findings become gating". Two problems with that recipe as written:

* Once the errexit bug above is fixed, the lint step ends in an unconditional `exit 0` on the findings path, so removing the registry entry makes the check-run GATE but the job still always succeeds on findings — the promoted gate would be vacuous.
* `scripts/check-advisory-registry.py` C2 requires that any job whose `name:` matches `\b(advisory|informational)\b` be declared in the registry. The job name is `actionlint (advisory)`, so deleting the entry without renaming the job REDs the registry checker.

So the documented promotion path is a three-part change, not a one-line deletion, and the criteria as recorded will mislead whoever performs it.
issues.fix_hint: Restate promotion_criteria as the full recipe: (1) change the lint step to `exit "$status"` (or exit 1 when findings > 0) instead of unconditional `exit 0`; (2) rename the job `name:` to drop the `(advisory)` token; (3) delete this registry entry; then confirm `python3 scripts/check-advisory-registry.py` is clean and update docs/branch-protection.md if the lane's gating posture is described there.
issues.title: promotion_criteria describes a promotion that would red CI: deleting the entry alone neither makes findings gating nor satisfies C2

issues.body:
actionlint shells out to `shellcheck` and `pyflakes` for `run:` step bodies and SILENTLY SKIPS those rule classes when the binaries are absent — it does not error. The lane's coverage therefore depends on the runner image (shellcheck ships on `ubuntu-latest` today; pyflakes is not guaranteed), and a future image change could quietly halve what this lane checks while it still reports "0 finding(s)".

Measured here on a box without shellcheck: `actionlint -no-color .github/workflows/*.yml` over the PR-head tree exits 0 with zero output, i.e. the shell-body rules contributed nothing and nothing said so. The existing self-test fixture only trips `syntax-check`, so it cannot distinguish "shellcheck ran and found nothing" from "shellcheck was missing".
issues.fix_hint: Either assert the integration is live — add a fixture with a `run:` body containing a deliberate shellcheck violation (e.g. an unquoted `$VAR` word-split) and require actionlint to report it — or explicitly disable those rules (`-shellcheck= -pyflakes=`) and say so in the header, so the lane's scope is stated rather than accidental.
issues.title: Self-test only pins the syntax-check rule, so silent loss of actionlint's shellcheck/pyflakes integration would go undetected

issues.body:
Two small hygiene points:

* `echo "$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"` prepends the whole scratch directory to PATH for every subsequent step. `$RUNNER_TEMP` is the shared drop-zone that other actions and steps write into, so anything later named like a system command there would shadow it. Low risk inside this two-step job, but installing to a dedicated directory costs nothing.
* `actionlint -no-color .github/workflows/*.yml` hard-codes `.yml`. The tree currently has no `.github/workflows/*.yaml` and no `.github/actions/**` composite actions, so nothing is missed today — but a future `.yaml` workflow or composite action would silently escape the lane, and `check-install-action-tool.py` already scans both extensions.
issues.fix_hint: Extract to `$RUNNER_TEMP/bin` (`mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin"; tar ... --directory "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin"; echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"`). For coverage, invoke `actionlint` with no path arguments (it discovers every workflow and composite action from the repo root) or glob `.github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml` with `shopt -s nullglob`.
issues.title: RUNNER_TEMP is prepended to PATH, and the lint glob misses future .yaml workflows

verdict.summary:
New advisory actionlint lane. Two blocking defects, both reproduced locally at the PR head.

1) The "advisory" lint step is not advisory. GitHub's default `run` shell is `bash -e {0}` (and `shell: bash` is `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}`). The step sets `set -uo pipefail`, which does NOT clear the inherited errexit, so the moment `actionlint ... | tee` returns 1 (findings) the script aborts at that line: `status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}` never runs, the exit-1-vs-exit-2 discrimination never happens, `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` is never written, and the step exits 1. Reproduced: `bash -e` over the exact step body exits 1 before the status check under both candidate shells. This falsifies the header claim "Exit 1 means lint findings and is reported without failing the job; actionlint invocation failures (exit 2/3) remain hard failures so a broken lane cannot look clean" — findings and tool breakage become indistinguishable, which is the specific failure mode the design says it prevents. The sibling self-test step gets this right with explicit `set +e`/`set -e`.

2) The `merge_group:` trigger is added without updating `docs/branch-protection.md` §Merge-queue subset, whose lane list is pinned set-equality-both-ways by `scripts/tests/test_mergequeue_lane_inventory.py`, run in `docs-quality.yml:995`. Ran it at the PR head: FAILED — "Triggers but undocumented: ['actionlint.yml']". That is a gating lane going red.

Verified good: the pinned sha256 `233b280d…7b4` matches the real actionlint 1.7.9 linux_amd64 tarball (downloaded and hashed); the self-test fixture is non-vacuous (actionlint 1.7.9 exits 1 on it, two syntax-check findings); `check-advisory-registry.py` is clean (C2+C3+C4) with the new entry; checkout is SHA-pinned with `persist-credentials: false` and `contents: read`.
